digest.component_or_area: test infrastructure: snapshot stall abort and ACLI subprocess timeout
propositions: Test slow progress validation serves real loopback remote with 15+ second wall time due to production ten-second low-speed window; contract requires sustained bytes above floor across one window, not elapsed time duration.

Test read retry with terminal failure uses one-second call timeout plus production backoff sleeps across three real child processes accumulating nine seconds wall time; contract is exactly three attempts, 2s/4s logical schedule, terminal timeout, and no surviving process group.

Injecting short test-only trigger windows (one second for slow progress, sub-second for ACLI) and recording retry schedule without sleeping will preserve real socket/process execution and semantic contracts while reducing per-test wall time to low single digits.
Production defaults for timeout, stall, grace, drain, attempt count, and backoff schedule must remain unchanged in code and behavior.
